title: On the numerical performance of finite-difference-based methods for derivative-free optimization
contribution: An 82-page handicapped benchmark showing that finite-difference gradients inside established codes (L-BFGS, lmder, KNITRO SQP) match or beat NEWUOA, DFO-LS and COBYLA on noiseless problems and stay competitive under noise, where the remaining gap traces to poor curvature (Lipschitz) estimates (read: arXiv:2102.09762v1, earlier title; OMS 2023 version not read).
problem_entry: The field's leading method (Powell-type model-based trust region, per Moré-Wild) is accepted first; the entry is the simple option the DFO literature dismissed without comparing against it, plus a practice/research split (practitioners use finite differences unwittingly) (arXiv pp. 4-5).
key_idea: No new algorithm: change only the derivative oracle (forward/central differences, interval from the noise level and a curvature estimate re-estimated when the step length is below 0.5) and one Armijo test (relaxed by 2 sigma_f), keep the solver engines unchanged (arXiv pp. 8-13, 22, 31).
assumptions: Smooth phi (C2 for constrained); additive i.i.d. uniform noise at four levels, the same for objective and constraints; noise level known or estimable; least-squares residuals evaluable individually, m residuals counted as one evaluation; two idealized estimates flagged (arXiv pp. 1, 7-8, 11, 13, 20, 23, 26).
proof_devices: No new theorem; Moré-Wild MSE bound (Theorem 2.1, cited) minimized over h to give the intervals (2.13)-(2.14) and the gradient noise orders used to explain central-difference accuracy (arXiv pp. 11-14)
Per-iteration linear-algebra counts, NEWUOA O(n^2) vs L-BFGS 4tn and DFO-LS O(mn^2) vs lmder O(mn), each backed by a CPU-time table over n (arXiv pp. 10, 22)

Failure computed by hand: DENSCHNE at x3 = -8 with sigma_f = 0.1 gives L about 6.705e-5, h about 20.539 and a derivative estimate about 3.791e9 against the true value about -6.707e-4; diagnosis is a pointwise L on a rapidly varying interval (arXiv p. 17)
Arms with idealized estimates (nine Hessian-based L schemes; Lipschitz exact to the true function for lmder) to separate estimator quality from the approach (arXiv pp. 23-24, 38-40)
experiments: 73 CUTEst unconstrained (n up to 300), 53 Moré-Wild least squares (n <= 12), 49 + 3 inequality-constrained CUTEst problems; log-ratio profiles of evaluations and optimality gaps; accuracy and efficiency reported separately; noise-free then four noise levels; exclusions and outcome classes explained; accuracy capped at 8 digits; rival at non-default settings in App. B; own L-BFGS memory set to 1; CPU tables; noise realizations per instance not stated (arXiv pp. 8-31, 42-44).
positioning: Accepts Moré-Wild's verdict on Powell's methods, builds on Berahas et al., Nesterov-Spokoiny and Moré-Wild [38], revives Gill et al. 1983; criticizes the DFO literature, the Larson-Menickelly-Wild survey and Cartis-Roberts for dismissing finite differences at the outset; credits NEWUOA and DFO-LS robustness under noise (arXiv pp. 4-7, 15, 21, 23).
writing: First-systematic-investigation claim, a counterfactual about the field's path, surprise flagged at each counterintuitive result, a Limitations section before the results, calibrated hedging; v1 slips: the abstract says equality constraints though the body tests inequality only, and Procedure I mislabels the RMS Lipschitz estimate (arXiv pp. 1, 4, 6-7, 11-12, 28, 41).
limits_future: Limits: one code per class, defaults, local and smooth only, one noise model, easy least-squares set, idealized central-difference M, parallelism argued but not measured, no conflict-of-interest statement despite an Artelys co-author. Future: robust curvature estimation (forthcoming [54]), NEWUOA under noise, nonsmooth finite differencing, noisy globalization (arXiv pp. 7, 10, 13, 15-16, 26, 32, 40).

method_links.note: Rivals taken from their community's benchmarks; DFO researchers consulted on the design. Own side handicapped: KNITRO L-BFGS memory 1, interior-point and SNOPT avoided as unfair to COBYLA, GALAHAD nls avoided. Termination aligned with COBYLA, the rival rerun at non-default settings, estimation costs counted, few codes, CPU paired with evaluations. Also bears out the recorded KNITRO platform/comparator limitation (Artelys co-author, no conflict-of-interest statement).

Step 7 and Taste mark 8 ('losses in the abstract'): in the v1 abstract no loss is stated; the loss (NEWUOA more efficient and accurate under noise) is in the section 1.2 contributions list. Later versions not read.

Dismissal of finite differences tested with the simplest h; the rule that an initial Lipschitz estimate suffices tested and rejected; surprise recorded; rival wins printed; verdict scoped and handed to other researchers to verify.

Only the derivative oracle and the Armijo test are changed; the estimate is driven by sigma_f and L re-estimated on the alpha_k < 0.5 trigger; step-length monitoring as the recovery signal (DENSCHNE); methods built as adaptations of existing codes. Page correction: the SKILL.md stop line's 'are not robust' is on p. 6 (section 1.2), not in App. A.

Partial: the paper ends with a register of open questions (curvature estimation, NEWUOA under noise, nonsmooth finite differencing, noisy globalization), one already assigned to the next paper [54]; no solver option exposed.
Least-squares structure treated as its own class with structure-exploiting codes on both sides; penalty reformulation with unconstrained DFO argued not to give a general-purpose method.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Run the method with exact or idealized values of the troublesome constant (Lipschitz exact to the true function for lmder; true-Hessian M; nine Hessian-based L schemes) to bound what a better estimator could gain and locate the gap in the estimator, not the approach.

Exclude non-comparable runs (initial sample hits the target, different minimizers, failures), sort constrained runs into four outcome classes, profile only the 32 that reached the same feasible point, explain the others problem by problem.

transferable: Log-ratio profiles of evaluation counts or optimality gaps, sorted across problems, for two-solver comparisons (arXiv p. 9)
Cap accuracy ratios with max{gap, 1e-8} so that ratios of tiny gaps do not mislead (arXiv p. 29)
Under noise, measure efficiency against the best value found by either solver, relative to the initial gap (arXiv pp. 15, 24, 31)
Tie the feasibility-failure threshold to the noise level, infeasibility >= sqrt(3 sigma_f) (arXiv p. 31)
Re-estimate curvature only when a cheap trigger fires (step length below 0.5) and count the evaluations used (arXiv p. 12)
Choose the variant of your own solver closest in spirit to the rival and state which stronger options were left out and why (arXiv pp. 19, 27)
Pair evaluation profiles with a CPU-time-versus-n table for one representative problem (arXiv pp. 10, 22)
Put a non-default study of the rival's parameters in an appendix (arXiv pp. 42-44)
Compute one failure of a parameter rule by hand: estimate, implied parameter, resulting error against the true value, broken assumption (arXiv p. 17)
coauthors: Hao-Jun Michael Shi, Melody Qiming Xuan (Northwestern IEMS), Figen Oztoprak (Artelys Corporation); Nocedal last author

quotes.text: We believe that if such comparisons had been made, particularly in the noiseless setting, research in the field would have followed a different path.
In other words, in the finite-difference approach to derivative-free optimization, algorithms do not need to be constructed from scratch but can be built as adaptations of existing codes.
